runs.note: The load rises from 2.75 to 4.04 during the two ONNX runs, which keep 4 threads busy themselves. These five were timed a second time because their first pass (15:24-15:26) overlapped another session's compile and a Python process at 100% CPU; the two passes pick the same and differ by at most 10% at p50 and 8% at p95 (the second is the slower one for the three Metal scorers).

Re-timed: the first pass (15:06-15:08) ran a pool binary that cargo had taken from the build directory ~/.cargo/config.toml shares between worktrees, built from another checkout's source, and it picked differently on 8 of the 480 cases. Rebuilt from this branch, both models give the accuracy run's scores exactly on every timed case, and 4.25M reproduces all 6317 picks of the accuracy run.

timing.load_note: 1-minute load average sampled every 20 s (every 5 s for the second and third runs); the idle desktop alone keeps it near 2; nothing else heavy (cargo, rustc, clang, mlx, training) was running at the start of any run

scorers.label: 本项目 4.25M int8
scorers.runtime: reference/examples/pool.rs (Rust reference implementation, CPU, one thread, SentenceModel::score with no state kept between decisions; context cut by MSIME's rerank_context)
scorers.fed: The context as MSIME hands it to its reranker: the committed text, its last 1024 bytes, cut by rerank_context in steps of 16 characters once it no longer fits the window. MSIME itself does not rerank the word cases: their pools are dictionary rows, which its gate leaves alone (trusted dictionary hit); there the row measures the model, not MSIME.
